security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI sets mseccfg.RLB=1 during boot PMP configuration (e.g., to merge/remove temporary rules or register executable shared-region rules) but subsequently fails to clear mseccfg.RLB=0 before handing off to the next boot stage. Per spec, RLB auto-locks at 0 only once a locked PMP entry (pmpcfg.L=1) exists; if OpenSBI's final PMP configuration contains no locked rules (e.g., only S/U-mode-only rules under Smepmp MML=1), RLB remains writable and set to 1 indefinitely, allowing any subsequent M-mode trap handler or SBI call path to modify or remove locked PMP entries, defeating the entire PMP protection.
security_spec.summary: OpenSBI uses RLB to configure PMP during boot but never explicitly clears it—RLB only auto-locks when a locked PMP rule exists, so if the final config lacks locked entries, RLB stays 1 and all PMP rules remain bypassable by any subsequent M-mode execution
